Priya / Arjun — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so engineering can kick off a light integration spike: 

Recap (what we covered)
- SDK quickstart (Node + Python) and server-side API options
- Auth choices: API keys for dev + short-lived mTLS/SAML for prod (we highlighted VPC Private option)
- Routing and model variants (latency vs cost tradeoffs)
- Structured output + tool-calling approach for your clinical-data extractor
- Embeddings + candidate reranker pattern for search use case
- Observability: trace ids, per-token latency headers, and per-route dashboards

Engineering asks / acceptance criteria for the spike
1) Get basic SDK auth working in dev (API key) and confirm request/response flow end-to-end
2) Add a trace_id to each user request and propagate to Redwood as an HTTP header (we recommend X-Redwood-Trace-Id)
3) Emit per-request latency headers from Redwood (X-Redwood-Latency-Total, X-Redwood-Latency-Model, X-Redwood-Latency-Network) and show them in a short CloudWatch/Datadog dashboard
4) Verify structured JSON output (tool-calling) for the extractor integration and a sample reranker evaluation on 100 queries
5) Share a short runbook with the exact logging field names and sample SDK snippet

Attachments: I attached a one-page telemetry playbook (redwood-telemetry-playbook-v1.pdf) and a sketch of the proposed arch (healthfirm-proposed-arch.drawio).

Proposed next steps
- Dev spike owner: Arjun (HealthFirm) + Dev: Dev Patel (Redwood) — sync this week
- We'll provide a small reference repo and a recommended set of headers/fields to log
- 30-minute tech sync: Thu 11/12 9:00 AM PT — confirm if that works

If that looks right I can loop in our platform engineer and share the reference repo + a short checklist.

Thanks — Sergio

Hi Priya / Arjun — adapting to your questions with concrete guidance below. I'll own the dev spike from our side and share a reference repo (small) before the sync.

1) Trace id mapping
- Recommended: send your existing x-request-id as X-Redwood-Trace-Id. Redwood will ingest either header; if both are present we forward both in logs as request_id and redwood_trace_id respectively.
- For correlation in your systems, we emit a log field named redwood.trace_id and we tag Datadog spans with "redwood.trace_id:<value>".

2) Latency headers & metrics
- Headers we return (per request):
  - X-Redwood-Latency-Total: 132ms
  - X-Redwood-Latency-Model: 120ms
  - X-Redwood-Latency-Preprocess: 8ms
  - X-Redwood-Latency-Postprocess: 4ms
- Metric prefix for histograms: redwood.request.latency (tags: route, model_variant, region, customer_id)
- We'll provide a Datadog dashboard JSON snippet you can import; the dashboard will parse the route and model_variant tags to break down tail vs p50/p95.

3) Structured output / model pinning
- For Dedicated/Private customers you can pin model versions; for hosted optional rollouts we include model_variant and model_sha fields on each response and in logs. Example response headers/log fields: model_variant: gptj-7b-q4b-v2, model_sha: 8f3d2a
- We also provide a response field redwood.rollout_reason when fallback occurs (e.g., capacity_fallback) so you can add an alert rule.

Reference SDK snippet (Node) — include X-Redwood-Trace-Id and print headers:

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
async function callModel(payload, traceId) {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'gptj-7b', input: payload }, { headers: { 'X-Redwood-Trace-Id': traceId } });
  console.log('response headers:', res.headers);
  // parse latency header
  const totalMs = res.headers['x-redwood-latency-total'];
  return res.body;
}

Runbook highlights I'll drop in the repo:
- Header names and example values
- Datadog import JSON and variable names (route/model_variant/customer_id)
- Minimal parsing helpers for Node/Python to capture trace id and latencies

I can push the repo and Datadog dashboard snippet by EOD tomorrow. Thu 11/12 11:00 AM PT works for me — I booked it tentatively.

Attachments I will share in the repo: redwood-telemetry-playbook-v1.pdf (updated), dd-dashboard.json
